title: Uniform twisted-pullback bounds and the domain of the tower projection formula
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a smooth separated morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e\geq1$, and put $R_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n=A_{E,en}$ for $n\geq1$. Use the ordinary derived categories of strict varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], their uniform constructible finite-Tor full subcategories $\mathcal C_T=\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], and ordinary derived tensor products [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Twists are [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and $F_\bullet=Rf_{!,\bullet}\dashv G_\bullet=f^!_\bullet$ with finite units, counits and evaluations is [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Put $\mathbf1_{\bullet,T}=(R_{n,T})_n$ and $\omega_\bullet=G_\bullet\mathbf1_{\bullet,Y}$, so $\omega_n=f^!_{R_n}R_{n,Y}$; pullback means levelwise finite derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Let $K_\bullet\in\mathcal C_Y$, and choose integers $a\leq b$ containing the Tor amplitude of every $K_n$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Suppose given an isomorphism $a_\bullet:\mathbf1_{\bullet,X}(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_\bullet$ whose finite levels are the diagonal orientations [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]. Put
$$P_\bullet=f_\bullet^*K_\bullet(d)[2d],\qquad Q_\bullet=f_\bullet^*K_\bullet\otimes^L\omega_\bullet.$$
Then each $f_{R_n}^*K_n$ is constructible with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Each $R_{n,X}(d)$ is a constructible locally free rank-one sheaf, including $R_{n,X}$ when $d=0$. The towers $P_\bullet,Q_\bullet$ are objects of $\mathcal C_X$ with cohomology and Tor amplitude in the common interval $[a-2d,b-2d]$, and the map induced by $1\otimes a_\bullet$ and twist reassociation identifies $P_\bullet$ with $Q_\bullet$.

The schemes $X,Y$ are Noetherian, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For every $n$ the finite Noetherian coefficient ring $R_n$ admits bounded constructible finite-Tor etale-origin witnesses for $K_n$ and $\omega_n$ (an etale-origin witness means a bounded constructible finite-Tor complex on the small etale site together with an isomorphism of its pro-etale inverse image with the given level). Both input towers $K_\bullet$ and $\omega_\bullet$ have common lower cohomological bounds, namely $a$ and $-2d$. Consequently the specified tower projection map for $(\omega_\bullet,K_\bullet)$ of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2a) exists and is invertible; its source and target, and $Q_\bullet$, lie in the domains needed to take its counit transpose under $F_\bullet\dashv G_\bullet$. No compatibility of the etale-origin witnesses across $n$ is required.

proof.text: Finite-type structure maps give Noetherian schemes; separation and quasi-compactness give qcqs. Coefficient ring finiteness and Noetherianity are the published instances. Apply [lem-sp-pullback-ordered-tate-bounds] to obtain pullback, line and ordered tensor bounds. Tensor the given orientation with the identity to obtain the actual isomorphism P to Q; transport bounds and membership through it.

Transport the original K level predicate along the published levelComparison. Test its assumed Tor interval against the coefficient unit, using a K-flat resolution and its tensor right unitor, to obtain cohomological support. Apply [lem-sp-uniform-bounds-origin-lower] independently to K and the oriented coefficient line, yielding both families of finite origins and ambient lower bounds.

Derive characteristic p from the finite-field datum. Apply the already stated tower compact-support projection formula to omega and realized K; this is the same specified SpTowerShriek.projection map. For its target use reverse ordered tensor bounds transported through the orientation, and the supplied hF preservation hypothesis. Conjugate through the realization counit. Transfer target membership back to the source along the projection isomorphism. Assemble the original Conclusion record; no unit step or diagonal orientation is reconstructed.
